relevance_note: The paper describes one identifiable girl with an HA20 diagnosis and a TNFAIP3 variant: "consistent with a diagnosis of Behçet-like autoinflammatory syndrome (HA20)", carrying "c.759delC: p. Asp253fs".
method_note: Single-patient case report plus brief literature review; read the whole Markdown file by hand, no script transcribed any table. In scope: only the one girl (label 'patient', rule 5); her parents appear only in the consent statement and as 'consanguine', so they get no rows, and no relative with individual-level facts is described. Cited cohort/survey papers (e.g. the systematic review of 177 cases) give only group counts, so they get no rows; no literature table of earlier patients is present. Table 1 is a two-pair parameter/result table for this patient only, with no ' / ' stacked cells. Variants in PIK3R1, HBB, SERPINA1 and the VPS37A VUS are named without any printed variant description, so no variant rows were created for them (v4, D-24); the paper itself says the TNFAIP3 variant 'remains the disease-causing mutation'. Contradiction found: the Abstract and Case Presentation call the TNFAIP3 variant 'likely pathogenic' while the Introduction (and later the Discussion, 'probable pathogenic variants') call it pathogenic; I recorded the 'likely pathogenic' wording in pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors and used the Case Presentation sentence as span. Parental Sanger confirmation was planned but 'delayed', so inheritance is 'not reported'. The Introduction statement that '~95% of affected individuals carry heterozygous TNFAIP3 pathogenic variants' is about affected individuals in general, not a named group including this patient, so zygosity is 'not reported'. Table 1 normal/negative results were recorded as phenotypic_features exclusions only where the paper prints a qualitative word (positive ANA, celiac serology, PPD, urine culture growth, low complement, abnormal urinalysis); the bare numeric laboratory values (WBC, ESR, AST, ALT, ferritin, BUN, creatinine, haemoglobin, platelets) were not turned into exclusions because the paper never labels them normal or abnormal. The negative MEFV testing is a genetic result, not a clinical feature, so it has no phenotypic_features row. The negative ANA is not used to mark the composite checklist item 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' as excluded (D-21, narrower than the item). The negative PPD and 'No growth' urine culture are not used for 'recurrent infections'. The paper gives no named-group statement covering this patient for checklist items, so checklist items are 'observed' only where the case description states the feature for her. Perianal swelling/tenderness and dysuria do not match any checklist feature and were left out of the checklist but kept in phenotypic_features. The checklist item 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' is 'not reported' even though diarrhea and perianal swelling/tenderness are recorded as features, because the paper describes the gastrointestinal evaluation as not showing findings suggestive of inflammatory bowel disease and only speculates that perianal involvement 'may represent an extension of gastrointestinal mucosal inflammation'. For the same reason 'central nervous system involvement' is 'not reported' although the infantile febrile seizure is recorded as a feature: the paper calls it 'a comorbid or coincidental event' and says no consistent reports emphasise such neurological complications in HA20.

the patient’s therapy was escalated to include infliximab, at a dose of 5 mg/kg administered at weeks 0, 2, and 6, followed by maintenance infusions every eight weeks.

span: Whole exome sequencing (WES) was performed (Whole Exome Sequencing was performed by NextSeq500, Twist Bioscience, San Francisco, CA, 100X, and Variant calling based on best practice of GATK.
